question: RAMP_TOKENS = 475 (contract.py, D3) was chosen as an interpolation between the 128- and 512-token columns of a calibration matrix taken with --enforce-eager, on the argument that at 128 tokens the per-request fixed costs are a large share of the reply. The 2026-08-24 sweep showed that flag was worth 5.02x on srv2, so the rate that argument was made against was 5x low there. Does the token budget still buy a throughput reading rather than an overhead reading when the per-request rate is what the rigs actually do with CUDA graphs on? Measured as: aggregate tok/s at n = 1, 16, 64, 128 for per-request budgets of 128, 256, 475 and 1024 tokens, on each rig's best-measured 1.5B configuration with max-model-len raised to 2048 so the 1024-token column fits. If 475 reads within a few percent of 1024 at every level, the budget is long enough under the new rate and D3 survives the re-derivation; if it does not, the constant moves and this run says to what.
arms: srv1, container vLLM 0.26.0, Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct-AWQ, --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --max-model-len 2048 --max-num-seqs 256, no --enforce-eager; four cells, one per token budget, one repeat per level.
srv2, the same with --kv-cache-dtype fp8 (the flag that produced its best cell; refused by compute capability on srv1).

Both rigs concurrently: each rig is the sole client of its own server (E14 is about a second claimant on ONE rig), and the client is this workstation, which the sweep already showed is not the bottleneck at these rates.

cost.estimate_note: srv1 is the long pole: four launches at ~120 s each with graphs on, plus levels whose wall is n*tokens/agg_tok_s -- the 1024-token column at n=128 alone is ~7 minutes at 296 tok/s. srv2 finishes in ~15 minutes.

could_have_carried: Four more graphs-on START_TIMEOUT_S points per rig, at --max-model-len 2048 rather than the sweep's 512-1024.
The n=1 fixed-cost share directly: latency at 128 tokens against latency at 1024 is two points on a line whose intercept is the per-request overhead.
left_on_table: Repeats. One repeat per level, so this cannot speak to RAMP_REPEATS; the cross-rig ramp's repeat_spread is the only spread on record and it is eager.
The knee ladder's dense low end. Levels are 1/16/64/128; a plateau read off these is at powers-of-two resolution.
Any model but the 1.5B, and any prompt but the sweep's short one.
prerequisites: tools/bench/serving/sweep.py with a per-cell `tokens` field (added in this lane for this run; the level's `tokens` was the level TOTAL and could not carry the per-request cap).
Both rigs idle at 1 MiB with no container of ours running -- confirmed before launch.
void_if: Either rig's launch refuses (a refused cell is written with its log and the column is missing, not zero).
A level records an error: sweep.py breaks the ramp at the first failed level, so a 1024-token cell that OOMs at n=128 has three levels, not four, and the README must say so.
A second client appears on either rig during a cell.
notes: Filed for #356, the RAMP_TOKENS box. sweep.py is in NOT_A_FIGURE (it states a throughput rate, not a pass rate) and still has no tests; this run does not change that.
